claim: Human judges given the same cases give very different outputs (insurer 55% median premium spread, 208 judges unanimous on prison in 3 of 16 cases, psychiatrists agree about half the time). All figures come via secondary summaries of the Noise book.
agent_test: none (motivation only); our own noise audit: same task, N samples, measure spread

claim: Noise splits into level, stable pattern and occasion noise; error = bias + noise. For an LLM, prompt format and example order act as pattern noise, resampling as occasion noise.
agent_test: Decompose variance on our agent: across prompts (pattern), across seeds (occasion), across model/personas (level)

claim: A model of bail decisions beat NYC judges: at the judges' release rate 24.7% fewer crimes; at their crime rate 41.8% fewer jailed. Stricter judges jail across the whole risk range, so part of the error is inconsistent ranking. Rules over cues beat judges' own use of them.
agent_test: Replace a model-judged step with a coded rule over extracted cues and compare accuracy at equal tokens. Caveat: selective labels, judges may weigh other goals.

claim: The Danziger hungry-judge effect (65% to ~0% favourable within a session) is contested: case order is non-random, the effect size (d near 2) is implausible, and a Ramadan study found the opposite. Do not cite as established occasion noise.
agent_test: No test; treat 'tired judge' as unproven. Test instead whether late-in-context calls degrade on our agent.

claim: LLMs configured to be deterministic (temperature 0) still vary: across 5 models, 8 tasks and 10 runs accuracy varies up to 15% across identical runs and the best-possible to worst-possible gap reaches up to 70% (Atil et al.). Separately, at ChatGPT's default temperature (1), 75.76%, 51.00% and 47.56% of CodeContests, APPS and HumanEval tasks had zero equal test output across five requests, and temperature 0 reduces but does not remove this (Ouyang et al.).
agent_test: Re-run the same item 10 times at temp 0 on our stack; report per-item accuracy range
audit_note: The ChatGPT code figures (75.76%/51.00%/47.56% of tasks with zero equal test output) are at the default temperature (1), not temperature 0, where non-determinism is lower but not zero; they also refer to equal test output, not equal text.
claim_before_audit: LLMs at temperature 0 are not deterministic: accuracy varies up to 15% across identical runs, best-worst gap up to 70% (5 models, 8 tasks, 10 runs); ChatGPT code tasks with no two equal outputs: 75.76%/51.00%/47.56%.

claim: Meaning-preserving prompt format changes move accuracy by up to 76 points (LLaMA-2-13B) and about 10 points on average across 50+ tasks; scale, shots and instruction tuning do not remove it, and format performance correlates only weakly across models. Instruction paraphrase also reorders model rankings: Kendall's W across templates ranges from about 0.27 to 0.91 over tasks (most below 0.85, i.e. weak to moderate agreement; Mizrahi et al.).
agent_test: Run K paraphrases/format variants of the scaffold prompts and vote; measure spread vs single format
audit_note: Sclar figures verified (76 points LLaMA-2-13B, ~10 average, 50+ tasks), but Mizrahi et al. Table 4 shows Kendall's W spanning about 0.27 to 0.91 across tasks, with most below 0.85 (weak to moderate agreement), not 0.71-0.91.
claim_before_audit: Meaning-preserving prompt format changes move accuracy by up to 76 points (LLaMA-2-13B), ~10 on average across 50+ tasks; scale, shots and tuning do not remove it; good formats transfer weakly across models. Instruction paraphrase also reorders model rankings (Kendall W 0.71-0.91).

claim: Few-shot example order alone moves accuracy from near state of the art to near chance, at all sizes 0.1B-175B, and good orders do not transfer between models.
agent_test: Shuffle example order across K samples in the loop; check spread

claim: Option position/label bias in multiple-choice: answer letter preferences move accuracy (llama-30B +15.2 points when answer is at its preferred slot, 20 LLMs). Permutation debiasing (PriDe) helps.
agent_test: Permute option order in code and average across permutations
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: LLM judges flip verdicts when answer order is swapped. Position consistency: GPT-4 65.0%, GPT-3.5 46.2%, Claude-v1 23.8% (Zheng); Vicuna-13B beat ChatGPT 82.5% vs 2.5% depending on order (Wang). Balanced position plus multiple evidence lifts GPT-4 human agreement 52.7% to 62.5%.
agent_test: Any pairwise comparison inside our agent: run both orders in code, count only consistent verdicts

claim: Same-input LLM judging is unstable across repeated runs: with sampling temperature 0.6, Krippendorff alpha over 3 runs was 0.326-0.788 on SummaC and 0.265-0.563 on MT-Bench (no model reached 0.8 on MT-Bench; Rating Roulette), and Lau (2026) found none of five judges (including GPT-4o and Claude Haiku/Sonnet 4.5) fully deterministic even at temperature 0. GPT-4 inter-sample alpha (0.587) is below human inter-annotator alpha (0.659) on SummEval (Stureborg et al.).
agent_test: Measure self-agreement of our own verifier/critic over 3-5 reruns; flag below ~0.8
audit_note: Numbers all verified, but the Krippendorff alpha values (SummaC 0.326-0.788, MT-Bench 0.265-0.563) were measured with sampling temperature 0.6 in Rating Roulette, so they do not show variation 'even when sampling is off'; only Lau (2026) tests temperature 0.
claim_before_audit: Same-input LLM judging varies across repeated runs even when sampling is off: Krippendorff alpha over 3 runs 0.326-0.788 on SummaC, 0.265-0.563 on MT-Bench; no model reached 0.8 on MT-Bench; GPT-4o/Claude-family judges not fully deterministic at temp 0 (Lau 2026). GPT-4 inter-sample alpha 0.587 below human inter-annotator 0.659 on SummEval.

claim: Majority vote of 3 judge runs beats the mean single run by 1-2.5 points (SummaC); 5 or 10 runs add nothing significant. Greedy decoding was worse than sampling+vote. Few-shot and CoT did not raise self-agreement. Clinical agent check: majority of 5 draws removed only 39% (CI 18-64) of the self-disagreement floor.
agent_test: Compare 1 vs 3 vs 5 judge samples at equal total tokens

claim: Averaging independent samples reduces LLM noise: self-consistency gains over greedy CoT GSM8K +17.9, SVAMP +11.0, AQuA +12.2, StrategyQA +6.4, ARC-c +3.9; sample-and-vote gains GSM8K +12 to +24%. Gains are smaller on easy tasks and cost scales linearly with samples. Verified against the arXiv PDFs.
agent_test: Equal-token test: N votes of a short chain vs one long chain

claim: Aggregation removes noise but not shared bias: samples from one model share errors (acquiescence above 50% in LLM forecasts, shared judge biases). Diverse models/personas are needed for independence. Newer: an all-models-wrong rate caps any vote or router at 1 minus delta (67 frontier models, delta 0.052 vs 0.023 predicted); self-agreement can reflect shared error on frontier models.
agent_test: Compare N samples of one model vs N from different prompts/models at equal tokens; measure error correlation
audit_note: Minor: Chen's paper names the quantity beta (not delta); Ding's shared-error check on Claude models is a small exploratory test (not significant for Opus, p=.07) run on a student-cohort dataset.

claim: An ensemble of 12 LLMs forecasts about as well as 925 human forecasters on 31 questions (Brier 0.20 vs 0.19, p=.85) but equivalence only within a wide 0.081 bound. Halawi: system Brier .179 vs crowd .149; ensembling helps only slightly (.1676 none vs .1651 median).
agent_test: Median-aggregate several forecasts at equal tokens and compare Brier to a single forecast
audit_note: Minor: the ensembling ablation (.1676 none vs .1651 median) is on the validation split where the human crowd scored 0.1600; the .179 vs .149 comparison is on the test set.

claim: Mean accuracy on multiple-choice is flat across temperature 0-1.0 (p=.403), so sampling noise hurts reliability more than average accuracy.
agent_test: Check on our tasks before paying for temperature 0

claim: Mixture-of-Agents (layered LLM refinement) reaches 65.1% (open-source) to 65.8% AlpacaEval 2.0 LC vs 57.5% for GPT-4o, but is scored by an LLM judge with the biases above and costs more tokens.
agent_test: Not at equal tokens in the paper; test against N-vote baseline

claim: Averaging two guesses from one person beats either guess, more so after a delay; asking oneself more than three times may hurt. Evidence is a secondary summary; the primary Vul and Pashler paper was not opened.
agent_test: Resample the same prompt with a different framing rather than the same one; compare to plain duplicates

claim: Mechanical combination of cues beats clinical judgment on average by about 10%, substantially so in 33-47% of studies versus clinical substantially better in 6-16% (Grove 2000 abstract, opened). A 2016 meta-analysis of lens-model studies finds the linear model of the judge beats the judge (Goldberg 1970 itself not opened). The earlier 46/48/6 split was wrong. No LLM-judge-versus-coded-rule test found.
agent_test: Test a coded rule (median of independent scored cues) against an LLM holistic verdict on one scaffold step

claim: At equal tokens, sequential refinement beat parallel majority vote in 43 of 45 open-model configurations (4096-token chains; AIME/GPQA), and debate or mixture-of-agents beat self-consistency by 1.3 to 2.7 points on MMLU-Pro at equal compute. No frontier closed-model equal-token test found.
agent_test: Compare on our own items at equal tokens: k short chains plus vote, one long chain, one chain plus a verifier call

claim: Self-agreement is a weak confidence signal on frontier models: Spearman 0.20-0.59 with majority-correctness; the most consistent model was over-confident but no more accurate; shared wrong answers had mean agreement 0.78-0.85. No fixed 85% threshold is justified.
agent_test: Use agreement to allocate extra samples, never to accept an answer; calibrate on our own data

claim: Errors are correlated across frontier LLMs: no vote or router can exceed 1 minus the all-models-wrong rate; at matched quality a diverse ensemble beats a Self-MoA one; the best fixed-budget forecast ensemble never uses a single model. Evidence is across models, not across prompts of one model.
agent_test: Measure the all-wrong rate across prompts of one model on 100 items before paying for more samples
audit_note: Minor: Chen's ceiling applies to policies that output one member's answer (route/vote/cascade), and the Self-MoA comparison is at matched quality; related work (Li et al.) reports Self-MoA often beats heterogeneous fusion in other settings.

claim: In a six-judge audit (GPT-5.2, GPT-4o, Gemini-2.5-Pro, Gemini-2.0-Flash, Claude-Sonnet-4.6, Llama-3.3-70B), 7-17% of verdicts changed across identical reruns at temperature 0 and order swaps flipped up to 98% of pairwise verdicts in the worst case (Gemini-2.0-Flash on JudgeBench); in a separate 21-judge study, test-retest reliability above 0.95 coexisted with position bias above 0.10 for some judges (Qwen3 8B, Gemini 2.5 Flash).
agent_test: Run every pairwise verdict in both orders in code; do not use repeat-agreement as the health check
audit_note: The 98% order-swap flip is a single Gemini-2.0-Flash cell (Verdict-first XML, JudgeBench), not a GPT-5.2, Claude-Sonnet-4.6 or Gemini-2.5-Pro result (their flip rates are far lower, e.g. Claude up to about 50%); the 7-17% rerun change and the >0.95 retest with >0.10 position bias (Qwen3 8B, Gemini 2.5 Flash) are otherwise supported.
claim_before_audit: Current judges (GPT-5.2, Claude-Sonnet-4.6, Gemini-2.5-Pro and others) still change 7-17% of verdicts across identical reruns at temperature 0 and flip up to 98% of pairwise verdicts on order swap; test-retest above 0.95 can coexist with position bias above 0.10.

claim: Rubric-based scoring has position bias too: criterion order alone flips the top-1 candidate on 15-41% of prompts; a few random orderings match balanced permutation.
agent_test: Randomise criterion order and take the median over 3 orderings

claim: Self-disagreement is not ordered by model size or vendor: a clinical agent changed its action in 2.5-23.7% of replicate pairs across six models. Hardware and batch changes alone moved a reasoning model's accuracy by up to 9%.
agent_test: Measure our own floor on 20 items x 10 reruns before any variant comparison
audit_note: Minor: Bellibatlu et al. state the no-ordering finding only for their 6-model panel and 16 synthetic vignettes, so it should be scoped to that panel; the 9% GPU/batch variation is for DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B in bf16 greedy decoding.

claim: Splitting a judgement into criteria did not beat a holistic multi-criterion prompt for pairwise judging (FLASK vs G-Eval). Kahneman's mediating assessments protocol has still not been tested on LLMs.
agent_test: Direct A/B test: independent sub-judgments with holistic call last vs holistic only

claim: Disagreement and order flips concentrate in near-tie pairs, so a flat self-agreement threshold misleads; give near-ties more samples or a coded tie-break.
agent_test: Stratify our reliability metric by score gap
